documents.title: Annihilation of Caste
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: An undelivered speech written for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal of Lahore. This is Ambedkar's most famous work — a searing critique of the caste system and Hindu orthodoxy.
documents.excerpt: You cannot build a nation on foundations of caste. You cannot build up a nation on principles of Hindu religion. Caste is not a division of labor, it is a division of laborers.

documents.title: The Constitution of India
documents.author: Constituent Assembly of India
documents.description: The supreme law of India, drafted by the Constituent Assembly with Dr. Ambedkar as Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Contains 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.
documents.excerpt: We, the people of India, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Democratic Republic and to secure to all its citizens...

documents.title: Who Were the Shudras?
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: A historical investigation into the origins of the Shudra caste. Ambedkar argues that Shudras were originally Aryans who were degraded to low status.
documents.excerpt: The Shudras were one of the Aryan communities of the solar race. They were originally Aryans. They did not form a separate varna but ranked as the third community in the Indo-Aryan society.

documents.title: The Buddha and His Dhamma
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: Ambedkar's final and most personal work. Presents the Buddha's teachings as a rational, scientific philosophy. Completed shortly before his own conversion to Buddhism.
documents.excerpt: The Buddha was nothing but a man. But he was a man who was the Enlightened One. He was the greatest man who ever lived.

documents.title: Riddles in Hinduism
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: A provocative critique of Hindu religious texts and practices. Published posthumously. Addresses contradictions in the Vedas, Manusmriti, and Bhagavad Gita.
documents.excerpt: The Vedas are a mere conceit, a farce. If the Vedas are to be believed, then the whole social fabric of Hinduism must go.

documents.title: Constituent Assembly Debates — Volume 1
documents.author: Constituent Assembly of India
documents.description: Proceedings of the Constituent Assembly debates, featuring Dr. Ambedkar's speeches on fundamental rights, directive principles, and the draft constitution.
documents.excerpt: The Draft Constitution as drafted by the Drafting Committee contains provisions which are liable to be questioned. But I need not dilate on them now.

documents.title: The Problem of the Rupee
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: Ambedkar's doctoral thesis from the London School of Economics. Examined the Indian currency system, gold exchange standard, and monetary policy.
documents.excerpt: The problem of the rupee is essentially a problem of the stabilization of its exchange value in terms of gold or sterling.

documents.title: States and Minorities
documents.author: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
documents.description: A memorandum submitted to the Constituent Assembly outlining safeguards for minorities. Proposed separate electorates and reserved seats.
documents.excerpt: The minorities in India have been subjected to the most cruel injustices and have been denied the most elementary human rights.
